name: Sly and Robbie
hook: Jamaica's most recorded rhythm section, who took the dub studio's logic of drum and bass as the song into reggae, pop, and hip-hop sessions worldwide.
blurb: Drummer Sly Dunbar and bassist Robbie Shakespeare started playing together at Channel One studio in Kingston in 1975. As the in-house rhythm section, they built new drum-and-bass patterns on hundreds of records, moving reggae away from rocksteady toward the more mechanical, bass-forward feel dub had been pointing toward. When they moved to Chris Blackwell's Compass Point Studios in Nassau, they took that sound out of Jamaica and into the centre of early-1980s crossover pop, on records by Black Uhuru, Grace Jones and many others, applying the same rhythm ideas to a much wider range of artists. The partnership ended when Shakespeare died after kidney surgery in December 2021. Dunbar died in Kingston in January 2026.

signatureTracks.title: Language Barrier
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Recorded with Bill Laswell in New York, this is Sly and Robbie stepping out from behind other artists to make the record under their own name.
